newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Orissa state privatises power distribution.
newsitem.headline: India's Orissa state privatises power distribution.

text.p: The government of the eastern Indian state of Orissa on Saturday handed over management of power distribution in central parts of the state to a private company, BSES Ltd, officials said.
BSES will distribute electricity to 500,000 customers in the state capital of Bhubaneshwar, and key towns of Cuttack and Dhenkanal, covering an area of 30,000 square km, they said.

"The management contract is aimed at improving the efficiency of operation, enhancement and reliability of supply, increasing customer satisfaction, reducing distribution loss, augmenting bill collection and revenue and overall improvement of the system," BSES' chairman R.V. Shahi told news conference.
Orissa has become the first state to undertake a major step under India's economic reform programme launched in 1991 to restructure its state-run electricity distribution services.
Low efficiency and uneconomic prices in state-run electricity boards have been major obstacles to foreign investors invited by India to meet its huge power shortages.
The Grid Corporation of Orissa, which replaced the state-run Orissa State Electricity Board, and BSES Ltd, signed the management contract on Friday, officials said.

BSES will receive basic management fees of 40 million rupees per year and performance-linked incentives on the basis of its success in reducing losses in power distribution, increasing revenue collection, and giving new connections, Shahi said.
